newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee gains sharply against forward dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee gains sharply against forward dollar.

text.p: The rupee gained sharply in the forward dollar market on Tuesday as banks went on a receiving spree (receiving premia against forward dollar), dealers said.
"Most banks were receiving," said a forward dealer at a leading European bank in Bombay. The movement was one-sided.
"Maybe some banks hit the stop loss trigger," he said.
Dealers reported genuine interest among exporters to receive premia and sell their dollar receipts forward.
July dollars closed at 1.46/1.48 rupees, down from the opening level of 1.51/1.54 rupees on Tuesday, dealers said.
The six-month annualised premium closed at 7.54 percent, down from the previous close of 8.03 percent, dealers said.
Easy liquidity conditions could have also contributed to the rupee's rise against the forward dollar, one dealer said.
Sluggish demand for dollars helped the spot rupee close at 35.845/852 on Tuesday. It had opened at 35.85/86 to the dollar.
Dollar supply was affected because banks in several cities in the south - Bangalore, Vishakhapatnam and Madras -- were closed for a holiday, dealers in Bombay said.
Dealers said they were at a loss to guess when the rupee would break out of the 35.85/95 per dollar range.

"The fundamentals warrant a depreciation (of the rupee against the dollar)," said a dealer. But the government, which is facing rising inflation and a ballooning oil subsidy deficit, would not want the rupee to weaken at this stage, he said.
"The two are managing the show well, but the fundamentals should assert itself before long," said a dealer, referring to the Reserve Bank of India and a leading state-run bank.
